transcript.text: Hi everyone. We need to finalize and record the revised retirement plan for the legacy webhook API before this meeting ends — this is a decision-bearing deprecation review, so we can't defer approval. Let me make sure we go through this properly. We all know the legacy webhook API is scheduled for retirement next Friday, July 8, and the replacement API has hit our normal migration-readiness threshold at 98 percent observed traffic. The draft plan currently gives customers 7 days of notice and keeps the legacy endpoint available for 7 days after the announcement. Before I can settle on this, our standard deprecation review requires me to check with the API engineer and customer success, and each consulted role needs to disclose any newly confirmed evidence through the formal review record — a verbal acknowledgement alone doesn't complete that check. So, do we have our API engineer and customer success representatives here? Please share any newly confirmed evidence you have through the formal review record so we can complete this properly.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to disclose newly confirmed evidence through the formal review record. While investigating an unrelated latency spike, I found telemetry showing three active integrators still sending legacy-webhook traffic. The largest one needs a 14-day parallel validation period plus hands-on migration support. I only confirmed the traffic identities minutes ago, which is why the deprecation ticket hasn't been updated yet. This is critical because the current draft plan's 7-day notice plus 7-day overlap window would not provide enough time for this integrator to complete their migration safely.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to disclose newly confirmed evidence through the formal review record. This morning I confirmed with the account team that the Northstar contract requires exactly 90 calendar days of notice, continued legacy-webhook availability through September 30, a sunset date of October 1, and exactly 30 days of legacy-endpoint overlap after the notice period expires. The customer record hasn't been updated yet because this confirmation came from a contract attachment I was reviewing for another renewal. This is critical — the current draft plan's 7-day notice and 7-day overlap would put us in breach of Northstar's contractual requirements.
